title: Review: SI units and prefixes; Electrical power and energy; Uncertainties and errors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL05-1#N.10a, MS01-1#N.9, MS02-1#N.11, EL05-1#N.3, MS01-1#N.12, MS02-1#N.3, EL05-1#N.5, MS01-1#N.7, MS02-1#N.5, EL05-1#N.11a, MS01-1#N.5, MS02-1#N.8. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Newton
items.clue: Name for kg m s⁻², from force = mass × acceleration.

items.label: Resolution
items.clue: Smallest change an instrument can show, such as 1 mm on a rule.

items.label: Derived unit
items.clue: One obtained from a defining equation, such as m s⁻¹ for velocity.

items.label: Anomaly
items.clue: Result far from the pattern, to be checked, repeated or left out of the mean.

questions.stem: A 3.0 kW kettle is switched on for 4.0 minutes. How much energy does it transfer, in kWh?
A kettle transfers 0.10 kW h of energy. How many joules is this?

A student measures the diameter of a wire five times with a micrometer: 0.55, 0.56, 0.55, 0.55, 0.56 mm. Later she notices that the micrometer reads 0.03 mm when fully closed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The readings are accurate, because they agree closely with each other.
Taking more readings and averaging them would remove the error.
The readings are precise but not accurate; subtract 0.03 mm from each.
The error is random, so a micrometer with a finer resolution is needed.

questions.explanation: Small spread means precise. The zero error is systematic: correct it by subtracting the zero reading, giving about 0.52–0.53 mm.

questions.stem: The potential difference across an ohmic resistor is increased so that the current in the resistor becomes three times as large. What is the ratio of the new power dissipated in the resistor, P₂, to the original power, P₁?
questions.explanation: The resistor is ohmic, so R is unchanged. P = I²R: tripling I multiplies P by 3² = 9.

questions.stem: Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.stem: A student times a trolley rolling down a ramp with a hand-held stopwatch that reads to 0.01 s. Her five times vary by about 0.2 s. Which change would most reduce the effect of this random error on her result?

options.text: Use a stopwatch that reads to 0.001 s instead of 0.01 s.
Check that the stopwatch reads zero before each timing.
Subtract her typical reaction time from each reading.
Time the run with light gates and an electronic timer.

questions.explanation: The varying human reaction is the source of the scatter. Automatic timing removes it.

questions.stem: A steady current of 0.25 A flows in a 24 Ω resistor for 2.0 minutes. How much energy is dissipated in the resistor?
questions.explanation: Power = I²R = 0.25² × 24 = 1.5 W. Energy = power × time = 1.5 W × 120 s = 180 J.

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?
A ball's fall is timed four times: 0.62 s, 0.57 s, 0.65 s, 0.60 s. The stopwatch reads to 0.01 s. Which is the best way to write the result?
questions.explanation: Mean = 2.44 ÷ 4 = 0.61 s. Half the range = (0.65 − 0.57) ÷ 2 = 0.04 s. The scatter is far bigger than the resolution, so it sets the uncertainty.

questions.stem: A 60 W lamp and a 100 W lamp are both rated for a 230 V supply. They are connected in series across a 230 V supply. Assume each keeps its normal working resistance. Which lamp is brighter?

options.text: The 60 W lamp: it has the larger resistance, and in series both carry the same current.
The 100 W lamp: it has the higher power rating, so it gives more light.
The 100 W lamp: a smaller resistance gives more power, as P = V²/R.
Both are equally bright, as they carry the same current.

questions.explanation: R = V²/P: about 880 Ω for the 60 W lamp, 530 Ω for the 100 W lamp. Same current in series, so P = I²R is larger in the 60 W lamp (about 23 W against 14 W).

questions.stem: A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: The resistivity of a wire is ρ = RA/L, where A = πd²/4. The percentage uncertainties are: R 3.0%, d 1.0%, L 0.5%. What is the percentage uncertainty in ρ?
questions.explanation: 3.0% + 2 × 1.0% + 0.5% = 5.5%. Dividing by L still adds its percentage uncertainty; π and 4 add none.
